messages:
oncall-bot: PAGER — GPU queue depth for dedicated pool 'ivanhoe' (tenant=TenetCorp) crossed critical threshold (90% queued). Auto-escalating to SRE + Infra.
Mila: I'm on it — seeing a steady rise in queued tokens and increasing tail latency in the tenant's routes. Confirming impact: TenetCorp requests timing out at ~10s for large prompts.
Jonah: Looking at node telemetry now. GPU utilization is at 98% on 6/8 nodes. Autoscaler has scale_limit=0 for this dedicated pool (per enterprise contract).
Tilly: If autoscale is disabled we can either enable a temporary burst override or redistribute lower-priority tenants. What's TenetCorp's SLA?
Alex_CS: TenetCorp has an enterprise SLA with priority routing; they are actively blocked on a regression test run. They're already on a remediation window. They want updates every 15m.
Mila: Quick mitigation suggestions: 1) Turn on burst override for 30m. 2) Reduce TenetCorp concurrency by 20% via soft throttling. 3) Failover a subset of TenetCorp traffic to their fallback model variant (smaller model) where acceptable. Which is fastest?
Jonah: Fastest is burst override — we have reserved burst capacity in region-2 but it requires infra approval. I can flip the flag: ``rctl dedicated.ivanhoe.burst_override=true --ttl 1800``.
Ops_lead: Approve temporary burst override for 30m to protect customer availability, but we need an executed rollback plan and cost ack from finance.
Mila: Approved. I'll run the override and put a short-lived rate limit on TenetCorp while we monitor.
Mila: (exec) ``> rctl set dedicated.ivanhoe.burst_override=true --by mila --reason 'tenet spike' --ttl 1800``
Deploy-bot: Deployment event recorded: burst_override=true applied by mila at 2025-06-12T14:40:15Z.
Jonah: After override, queuing dropped from 92% -> 45% in ~90s. Tail latency improving. Still seeing 2 nodes with high mem pressure.
Tilly: Can we evict any non-critical workloads from the pool? There are two non-prod tenants marked 'best-effort'.
Jonah: Yes — I'll trigger eviction for best-effort tags. Command: ``> infra-ctl drain --pool ivanhoe --tag best-effort``.
Jonah: (exec) draining best-effort -> freed ~16% GPU cycles, effective immediately.
Alex_CS: Messaging TenetCorp now: "We're activating temporary capacity and throttling to stabilize. ETA initial recovery: 5-10 minutes. Will follow up with root cause once stabilized."
Mila: Good. I'll start a 5-minute cadence check. Triage notes: queue spike correlated with a batch of 1200 concurrent long-sequence eval runs from TenetCorp at 14:32 UTC. Looks like a scheduled run that didn't respect the concurrency cap.
Ops_lead: For follow-up we need: a) reproduce the schedule in test, b) add a guard to limit single-tenant burst, c) confirm updating customer runbook with concurrency guidance. Assigning next actions.
Mila: Handoff — I'm going offline in 20m. Jonah, take primary ownership for the mitigation window and post status updates. Tilly, you're secondary for postmortem duties.
Jonah: Taking over. Current status: burst on, best-effort drained, throttling policy applied (soft_drop=20%). Monitoring logs for retries/errors.
Deploy-bot: Incident annotation: mitigation_steps=[burst_override, drain_best_effort, soft_throttle] by mila/jonah at 2025-06-12T14:43:05Z.
Tilly: I'll collect metrics for the postmortem: per-node GPU util, queue depth, request latency P50/P95/P99, and TenetCorp request distribution.
Mila: Last thing — set a calendar reminder to review contractual autoscale exceptions for TenetCorp and determine permanent capacity adjustments.
Jonah: Will do. Next update in 10m.
Mila: Thanks team.
Jonah: 10m follow-up: system stable, queue <20%, tail latency back to baseline. I'll keep monitoring and will start a ticket to enforce concurrency caps on TenetCorp's tenant config.
Alex_CS: Sent customer note: "Stability restored, we applied temporary capacity and throttling. We'll share a post-incident report within 48 hours."
Tilly: Adding action items to postmortem: R1 - autoscale option review; R2 - tenant-side concurrency enforcement; R3 - alert tuning for earlier signal; R4 - billing review for burst costs.
Mila: Closing loop — handoff complete, leaving note in pager: 'jonah active'.
Jonah: Acknowledged.
Mila: (automated) On-call shift ends for mila at 2025-06-12T15:00:00Z.
oncall-bot: Incident thread marked "monitoring". If regressions appear, re-open page with /page incidents."
